title: Eval-driven safety circuit for phased config/model changes
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement an automated safety circuit that evaluates live canary and A/B experiments against targeted quality signals and enforces automatic rollback or traffic adjustments when regressions exceed configured tolerances. This ticket covers the evaluation orchestration, decision logic, SLO/metric mapping, and a deterministic rollback actuator that can be exercised by both Hosted and Dedicated deployments.

We will not change model binaries here; the focus is on config-driven rollouts (prompt templating, decoding parameters, quantization profiles, kernel selection toggles) and model swaps where the replacement is compatible (same architecture and KV cache format).
background:
We currently have manual eval dashboards and several canary guards that require human intervention. Past incidents show subtle config changes (beam size, sampling temperature, KV cache eviction) produced regressions in specific cohorts. We need a machine-readable, repeatable safety circuit that: (1) continuously scores canary/A-B cohorts against curated eval sets and production holdout traces; (2) accounts for sample variance and traffic volume; and (3) executes safe, auditable rollback actions when triggered.

Related tickets in the backlog focus on cohort sampling and metric collection; this ticket is the orchestration and policy layer that ties metrics to actions.
proposal:
1) Evaluation engine: wire live canary/A-B cohorts to an evaluation pipeline that computes per-cohort metrics every minute: prompt-rewrite match rate, hallucination rate, task-specific accuracy (where available), token-efficiency, latency P95, and error rate.
2) Statistical decision rules: use sequential analysis (e.g., SPRT or Bayesian credible intervals) to determine significant regressions given current sample size and traffic. Define configurable guard thresholds per metric (absolute or relative deltas).
3) Policy actions: graded actions: reduce canary traffic by X%, disable the config flag (rollback to baseline), or fully revert to previous model. Actions must be idempotent and logged to audit trails.
4) Safeguards: require minimum sample sizes, tie-breaker holdout evals, and optional human-in-the-loop approvals for high-impact rollouts.
5) Integrations: Console rollout API, routing controller, audit log (for Private), and the eval metrics store.
6) Observability: per-rollout runbooks, a dedicated dashboard, and alerting rules that reflect both transient flaps and sustained regressions.
success_criteria:
- Canary/A-B run will automatically trigger a graded action within SLO when a guarded metric violates thresholds with high statistical confidence.
- Reversion semantics are deterministic and revert exactly the change applied (config or model version).
- No false-positive full reverts in 30-day randomized dry run window (target false positive rate < 2%).
- Operators can see a complete audit trail: metric snapshots, statistical test outputs, and action execution logs.
- Integrations tested in Dedicated staging and Hosted sandbox environments.
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end test: run a simulated canary with an injected regression and observe traffic ramp-down and final rollback; verify audit trail entries and console UI state.
2) Statistical engine: unit tests for SPRT/Bayesian decision boundaries and deterministic behavior under varying sample sizes.
3) Rollback actuator: idempotent API that can toggle config flags or swap model version and has a fallback if API fails.
4) Dashboard: shows live cohort metrics, decision confidence, and action history.
5) Security: rollback actions require service token with scoped permissions and are recorded in the audit log.
6) Documentation: runbook and run-through added to the Console docs and internal runbooks folder.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): implementation in staging with synthetic regressions and dry-run mode (no actuations). Phase 1 (limited): enable graded traffic adjustments for low-risk configs (non-model binary changes) for 1% of traffic across multiple tenants. Phase 2 (expanded): allow full rollbacks for pre-approved customers and Dedicated clusters. Phase 3: promote to default behavior with optional human approval gates for enterprise tenants. Each phase runs for at least 2 weeks with monitored metrics.
monitoring_playbook: If an automated rollback fires: 1) on-call receives alert with run ID and metrics; 2) system posts rollback reason and affected tenants to Slack channel #rollout-safety; 3) operations reviews the audit trail and, if safe, replays the rollout with adjusted thresholds or aborts further rollouts; 4) postmortem created if customer impact > low. Include checklist for manual rollback reversal, and contact list for affected account owners.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for eval metric calculations and statistical tests.
- Integration tests: simulated traffic harness that drives canary/A-B cohorts with controlled perturbations.
- Chaos tests: inject delays/failures in metrics store and ensure actuator has safe default behavior.
- Shadow runs: run the decision engine in shadow on 100% of traffic for 30 days to measure false positive/negative rates before enabling actuations.
notes:
Key engineering trade-offs: simple thresholding reduces cognitive load but increases false positives; sequential tests reduce required sample sizes but add complexity. We'll start with a conservative Bayesian credible-interval approach with monotonic guards and iterate. Ensure actions are reversible and small (traffic percentage reductions) before full reverts.

Privacy: no raw user prompts are kept in the eval store; use hashed prompt fingerprints and synthetic repros for audit.

Operational constraints: Dedicated tenants may restrict automated actuations; provide an opt-in enterprise policy.
